meta.fullName: Thailand Innovative G-force Varied Emulsification Research for Space Exploration
meta.title: TIGERS-X — A microgravity emulsification laboratory in 4U
meta.description: TIGERS-X is a teleoperated lab-on-chip cube that recorded oil–water mixing in Tesla-valve microchannels during a 10-day campaign aboard the International Space Station.
meta.ogImageAlt: The TIGERS-X payload floating inside a station module.

hero.name: TIGERS-X
hero.fullName: Thailand Innovative G‑force Varied Emulsification Research for Space Exploration
hero.lead: TIGERS-X is a low-cost, teleoperated lab-on-chip cube. For {days} days aboard the International Space Station it recorded how an immiscible oil and an aqueous phase redistribute in Tesla-valve microchannels under sustained microgravity. After installation, every science run was commanded from the ground.

science.heading: Emulsification without buoyancy
science.intro: Lipid emulsions used in intravenous nutrition are made on Earth by high-shear mixing. Turbulence breaks the oil into droplets, and buoyancy separates or stabilizes the phases. Neither mechanism is available in microgravity, where interfacial tension and capillary forces dominate. TIGERS-X tested whether a passive Tesla-valve mixer can still redistribute an immiscible oil–water pair under those conditions. The flight measured mixing behavior. It did not manufacture a medicine.
science.aimsHeading: What the flight was built to answer
science.aimsIntro: The campaign links three results: a cube qualified for the station, a record of oil–water flow over days rather than seconds, and a teleoperated platform later experiments can reuse.

tpn.title: A mixer that does not need shear or buoyancy
tpn.body: Parenteral emulsions are specified by droplet size. Conventional production uses high-shear homogenizers. TIGERS-X asks whether capillary instabilities in a static mixer can redistribute the phases when those homogenizers cannot be used.

food.title: Sustained microgravity, not a brief parabola
food.body: A 2025 parabolic-flight study saw stronger interfacial mixing, but each interval lasted about 20 seconds and included g-jitter. The station campaign follows the same class of passive mixing for long enough to see how the flow develops and then rests.

medicine.title: A platform for the next experiment
medicine.body: After installation the cube needed no crew. The same teleoperated architecture is a route to more demanding microgravity life-science work, including cell-culture systems, on later flights.

platforms.title: From parabolic flight to orbit
platforms.intro: The same group first measured passive mixing on parabolic flights. Those intervals were too short, and too disturbed, to show how a mixture evolves. The station campaign was designed to close that gap. The cube that flew is described next.
platforms.caption: Parabolic-flight experiment compared with TIGERS-X on the ISS
platforms.note: Parabolic-flight values are from Seehanam et al., Scientific Reports (2025), as cited in the TIGERS-X preprint.

inside-4u.title: A laboratory in 4U.
body: Eight pumps, eight fluid bags, two lab-on-chip devices, four cameras, and the computers that sequence them occupy a cube 200 mm across. The following views open that cube. Qualification and the flight come after.

envelope.title: Compact in design
body: The cube follows the ICE Cubes interface: 200 × 200 × 100 mm, a 4U volume. Mass at pre-flight handover was 2.32 kg, or 2.52 kg with the launch bag. It draws power and data from the facility.

structure.title: One structure, two modules.
body: The frame is aluminium 7075. An internal panel separates the experiment module from the electronics module. Removing the panels shows how the parts are arranged.
This exploded view is an assembly diagram. The cube does not open this way in flight.

fluidics.title: Metered delivery, double containment.
body: Eight Takasago RP-QIII peristaltic pumps move fluid by compressing tubing. Each of the four channels has one pump for the oil phase and one for the aqueous phase.
Eight CryoStore bags share one reservoir: two oil-phase bags of 10 mL, two BFluid® bags of 15 mL, and four collection bags of up to 25 mL. The circuit is sealed and double-contained.

observation.title: Four cameras, one corrected view.
body: Four See3CAM cameras in a 2 × 2 array sit beneath the chip and image it under white LED illumination. Each camera covers part of a device, so synchronized pairs are stitched into one panorama. The chip is lifted here only to show the cameras.
A four-color reference swatch in every frame supplies the correction for illumination differences between sessions.

computing.title: Onboard control between contacts.
body: An Orange Pi 5 Pro decodes telecommands, sequences each run, and stores images and telemetry. An onboard YAMCS instance buffers data while the station is out of contact. Pump and lighting commands are passed to an STM32F746 microcontroller.
The facility provides a single 12 V supply, regulated onboard to 5 V and 3.3 V.

core.title: Four channels on two devices.
body: Fluid handling, imaging, and computing exist to run the lab-on-chip: two Tesla-valve devices, CH1 and CH2, each with two parallel rows. That is four independent mixing channels.

deliver.title: Two immiscible, optically distinct phases.
body: Each channel receives Fluid A, an oil-phase mixture colored with oleoresin paprika, and Fluid B, BFluid® colored with a food-grade blue dye. On camera the oil reads orange and the aqueous phase teal. The dyes make the phases measurable by hue. They are not the mixture under study.

mix.title: The geometry does the mixing.
body: The Tesla-valve chain is a passive static mixer. There is no impeller and no high-shear homogenizer. The pumps maintain the flow; the channel shape redistributes the phases.
Twelve fittings on the underside connect the chip to the circuit: two inlets and one outlet for each of the four channels.

watch.title: Hue as a measure of composition.
body: Video from each cycle is downlinked and examined the same day. Each frame is hue-corrected against its reference swatch.
A pixel is then scored from 1, a water hue, to 2, an oil hue. Interfacial and partly mixed regions take intermediate values, so the index does not impose a hard boundary between the phases.

time.title: What changes when buoyancy is removed.
body: Microgravity suppresses buoyancy-driven separation. Viscosity and interfacial tension remain, and the two phases do not become miscible.

The on-orbit images show how that balance developed. Both devices began alike, then diverged. The sequence and the mixing index are reported with the science operations, after the cube is on the station.

chip.title: Lab-on-chip
chip.description: Two devices, CH1 and CH2, each with two parallel Tesla-valve rows. Each channel has an oil inlet, an aqueous inlet, and one outlet. The valve chain folds the phases together, then opens into an observation chamber.

pumps.title: Eight peristaltic pumps
pumps.description: Takasago RP-QIII peristaltic pumps move fluid by compressing tubing. Each channel has one pump for the oil phase and one for the aqueous phase.

reservoir.title: Fluid storage
reservoir.description: Eight CryoStore bags in one container: two oil-phase bags of 10 mL, two aqueous bags of 15 mL, and four collection bags. The circuit is sealed and double-contained.

cameras.title: Four cameras
cameras.description: Four See3CAM cameras in a 2 × 2 array image the chip under white LED illumination. Synchronized pairs are stitched into one panorama.

computing.title: Computing and control
computing.description: An Orange Pi 5 Pro sequences each run, stores images and telemetry, and buffers data in onboard YAMCS. It commands an STM32F746 microcontroller, which drives the pumps and the LED illumination. A USB hub powers the four cameras.

structure.title: Structure and enclosure
structure.description: An aluminium 7075 structure carries the subsystems inside a 200 × 200 × 100 mm envelope. Internal parts use their own materials.

connector.title: Facility connector
connector.description: A DB13W3 connector on the underside mates with the ICE Cubes Facility. The cube draws +12 V only. Four differential pairs carry Gigabit Ethernet for commands and data.

flow.svgTitle: Oil and water phases flowing through one Tesla-valve channel
flow.svgDesc: Outline of one channel row on the flight chip. The aqueous and oil phases enter from the inlets on the left, pass the Tesla valves, cross the observation chamber, and leave through the outlet on the right. The motion is illustrative, not a measured velocity field.
flow.caption: One of four channel rows, traced from the flight-chip geometry. The channels are 1 mm deep. Flow in the figure is illustrative, not a measured velocity field.
flow.follow: The Tesla valve is a passive static mixer with no moving parts. Asymmetric branches divide the stream, return part of it, and rejoin it at an angle, so the phases are driven into one another. The path then opens into the observation chamber.

stages.title: Inlets
stages.text: Two pumps feed this channel. BFluid® enters along the outer edges and the oil phase enters along the centerline. The streams remain side by side until the valve chain.

stages.title: Tesla valves
stages.text: The streams enter a passive Tesla-valve chain. The pumps maintain the flow. Mixing is produced by the channel geometry.

stages.title: Chamber
stages.text: The channel opens into a rectangular observation chamber. This is the field recorded by the cameras.

stages.title: Outlet
stages.text: Effluent leaves through the outlet fitting and is collected in that channel’s bag.

mission.title: Qualified before flight.
mission.lead: The cubes were designed and built entirely by Thai engieers and scientists. Fluids were prepared under sterile conditions in a class II biosafety cabinet, then sealed for flight.
mission.qualifyIntro: Before handover the cube was verified against the ICE Cubes interface requirements and the safety requirements for pressurized ISS payloads.
mission.structure: Mechanical loading and vibration on all three axes, at Thailand’s Electrical and Electronic Products Testing Center (PTEC). Inspection before, during, and after each run found no cracking, loose parts, or change in structural signature.
mission.chem: NASA assessed every reagent, including the trace colorants, as non-corrosive, non-oxidizing, and non-flammable at the quantities flown. If both containment layers failed together, the releasable volume would be at most about 60 mL.

launch.title: Launch and installation
launch.transport: The cube was transported unpowered. It launched on {launch} on {vehicle} from {launchSite}.
launch.afterDocking: After docking, a crew member installed the cube in the ICE Cubes Facility in Columbus. That single interface provides power, data, and grounding. The User Home Base in Bangkok then completed remote commissioning. From that point the science runs required no further crew involvement.

steps.title: Installed in Columbus.
body: TIGERS-X operated in Columbus, the European Space Agency laboratory module, on the starboard side of the Harmony node.

steps.title: A rack-mounted laboratory.
body: Columbus supplies power, thermal control, and communications to the facilities in its racks. ICE Cubes is one of those facilities.

steps.title: The ICE Cubes Facility.
body: Operated by Space Applications Services, the facility accepts compact experiment cubes inside the pressurized module. Each cube connects once, for power and data.

steps.title: Crew time limited to two events.
body: The crew installed the cube and removed it at the end of the campaign. Between those events the experiment was commanded from the ground, as the path below shows.

command.title: Telecommand and telemetry
command.lead: Commands left the User Home Base in Bangkok on YAMCS. Video and logs returned along the same path.
command.note: The moving point traces the command path. It is not a record of the radio signal.

stages.title: The command leaves Bangkok
stages.text: The Chulabhorn Royal Academy User Home Base issues a telecommand in YAMCS. A VPN carries it to the ICE Cubes Mission Control Centre in Belgium. The cube has no radio of its own.

stages.title: The station link
stages.text: Space Applications Services places the command on the station’s space-to-ground link. The link is available only during acquisition of signal, so a command waits when the station is out of contact.

stages.title: Delivery in Columbus
stages.text: The ICE Cubes Facility delivers the command over Gigabit Ethernet, on the same interface that supplies the cube’s 12 V.

stages.title: The run is executed onboard
stages.text: TIGERS-X executes the commanded cycle. No crew action is required.

stages.title: Video and logs return
stages.text: At the end of the cycle, video and logs leave along the same path. Between signal windows, the onboard YAMCS instance stores the files and retains the experiment state.

stages.title: Analysis the same day
stages.text: The files arrive at the User Home Base by secure transfer. Preliminary analysis begins the same day.

operations.title: Flow behavior in the channels.
operations.lead: Over ten days the chip was imaged under sustained microgravity. The sequence is the qualitative record. The mixing index is the quantitative one.
paragraphs: Every science cycle was commanded from Bangkok through YAMCS. Eight pumps metered the oil and aqueous phases into four Tesla-valve channels, CH1 and CH2, each with two rows. Paired camera views were stitched into one panorama, and an in-frame color swatch corrected each session. Video and logs were downlinked after each cycle and examined the same day.

At event 1, both devices showed the same front: oil leading, the downstream channel still empty. By event 2 they had diverged. Water penetrated the serpentine path of CH1, while CH2 remained largely oil. At events 3 and 4 the split was sharper. In CH1 the aqueous phase occupied most of the visible channel and oil was confined to the rim. In CH2, oil occupied most of the length and water remained near the inlet.

The cumulative mixing index, from 1 for a water hue to 2 for an oil hue, converged within the first {convergedWithinPct}% of channel length in all four rows and then remained nearly flat. At event 4 the outlet values were {ch11} and {ch12} on CH1, and {ch21} and {ch22} on CH2. The CH1 rows were nearly symmetric. The CH2 rows were not. Pumping maintained the flow. The channel geometry set the phase distribution.

return.title: Recovery
return.body: After the campaign the crew removed the cube. It was deactivated and returned on a cargo vehicle. On the ground it is powered on again so that post-flight measurements can be compared with the on-orbit data. That comparison is the third stage of the concept of operations, and it is still in progress.

record.title: Operational record.
record.lead: The mixing results above come from the imagery. The figures here are the operational account: how long the cube ran, and how much it recorded, commanded, and returned.
record.note: Science operations ran from {operationsStart} to {operationsEnd}, within the available acquisition-of-signal windows. A power interruption of about {powerInterruptionHours} hours did not compromise the campaign.
record.barAria: {downlinkedGB} GB of approximately {recordedGB} GB recorded was downlinked before physical retrieval, about {percent} percent.
record.pumpNote: The pumps did not run continuously. Across {pumpOperations} operations their combined runtime was 15 min 22 s.
record.caveat: These figures are from the team’s mission report, not from the mixing analysis. They record that the payload accepted commands, moved fluid, stored imagery, and returned data, with no crew involvement beyond installation and removal.
